question: What is the IUPAC name of allylamine which is used to make pharmaceuticals and other chemicals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2-Propen-1-amine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allylamine**:-

 
 
• It is a primary amine with the chemical formula C₃H₅NH2.
 
• It is a colorless liquid with a pungent odor and is highly soluble in water.
 
• Allylamine is used in the production of a wide range of pharmaceuticals, including antihistamines, antifungal agents, and anticancer drugs.
 
• It is also used in the manufacture of various chemicals, including pesticides, resins, and plastics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Propan-1-amine:-**

 
 
• It refers to a different compound with a different molecular structure.
 
 
 
• **Benzenamine:-**
 
 
• It refers to an entirely different compound with a benzene ring in its structure.
 
 
 
• **N-Methylethanamine:-**
 
 
• It refers to a compound with a different molecular formula and structure.
